title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is from the post-Esquisse 'Longue Marche' sequel, studying Galois actions on the profinite fundamental group of U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞} over Q and on its Fermat (maximal-abelian geometric) quotient.

Notation.
- M^{!et}_Q is the arithmetic étale fundamental group of U_{0,3,Q}. It is an extension of Γ_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q) by the geometric group π_1(U_{0,3,Qbar}), written M_{0,3}^!.
- G_{p,σ}^♮ ≅ Ẑ^*·M^ is the quotient of M^{!et} cut out by the Fermat tower. The geometric part is abelianized, so G_{p,σ}^♮ is a semidirect product Ẑ^* ⋉ M^. Here M^ ≅ Ẑ(1)^2, the abelianized geometric π_1 (equivalently T_∞(G_m)⊗M with M = Z^3/diagonal or its sum-zero dual). Ẑ^* acts through the cyclotomic character. So G_{p,σ}^♮ sits naturally inside Aff(M^).
- N_σ^♮ ≅ Ẑ^*·Ẑ is a sub-semidirect product, presumably the normaliser-type piece attached to σ, embedded in Ẑ^*·M^ (diagonally, as it turns out).

The commutative square (328).
- Top row: Γ_Q ⊂ Π_Q^{et} → N_σ^♮. This is the homomorphism (326) that Grothendieck wants to make explicit arithmetically.
- Left vertical arrow: the section κ_{1/2} of M^{!et} → Γ_Q given by the rational base point 1/2.
- Bottom row: the 'Fermat' projection M^{!et} → G_{p,σ}^♮.

Meaning.
- (329) Γ_Q → Ẑ^*⋉Ẑ is read off from (330) Γ_Q → Ẑ^*·M^ ⊂ Aff(M^). This is the Galois action on the fibre of the Fermat tower at the rational point 1/2.
- That fibre is a torsor under T_∞(G_m) ⊗_Ẑ M^.
- Hence σ ↦ (χ_cyc(σ), Kummer cocycle of the coordinates of the point).

Computing the coordinates.
- Grothendieck uses his isomorphism Ψ (317) between U_{0,3} and the line U_1 = {x_0+x_1+x_∞ = 0} in G_m^3/G_m ⊂ P^2.
- The point 1/2 goes to (-1/2, -1/2, 1). The page writes the last coordinate as -1 (a slip); the next page has +1, which is forced by the sum being 0.
- The next page completes this: U_∞(s_{1/2}) ≅ T_∞(-1/2) × T_∞(-1/2).
- So the Galois image is σ ↦ (χ(σ), κ_{-1/2}(σ), κ_{-1/2}(σ)), where κ_{-1/2} is the Kummer character of -1/2 (essentially of 2, up to the sign/2-torsion part).
- The two translation components coincide. That is why the image lies in a diagonal copy Ẑ^*⋉Ẑ ⊂ Ẑ^*⋉M^, which explains the embedding N_σ^♮ ⊂ Ẑ^*·M^.

What it serves: describing 'arithmetico-geometrically' the abelian (Fermat-level) shadow of the Galois action on π_1 of P^1 - 3 points via a symmetric rational base point. It is a sanity-check / explicitation step in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme.
errors: The point in U_1 is written (-1/2,-1/2,-1); it must be (-1/2,-1/2,1) so that the sum is 0, as the next page correctly writes.
Minor: the text says the fibre at 1/2 is explained 'by the hom (326)', but the logical direction is the reverse: (326)/(329) is deduced from (330). This is harmless.

ideas.what: Galois action on the fibre of the Fermat tower (abelianized geometric π_1 of P^1-{0,1,∞}) at a rational point is given by cyclotomic character plus Kummer characters of the point's coordinates; image in the affine group Ẑ^*⋉Ẑ(1)^2
ideas.modern_name: Abelian (Kummer) part of the outer/pointed Galois representation on π_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}); Fermat curve tower as maximal abelian cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory; framed for the Fermat tower by Ihara (1986, Annals, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'), Anderson, Deligne (1989)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as such, to my knowledge (unsure).

ideas.what: Use of the symmetric rational base point 1/2 (fixed by z↦1-z) as a section κ_{1/2} of the arithmetic π_1, and its matching with the point (-1/2,-1/2,1) on the line x_0+x_1+x_∞=0 in G_m^3/G_m
ideas.modern_name: Rational base point sections of π_1(P^1-3 points) and the associated Kummer cocycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Ihara, Deligne, Nakamura on rational/tangential base points)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine explicitation: the Galois image at the Fermat (abelian) level for base point 1/2 is cyclotomic plus Kummer characters of -1/2. This is standard Kummer theory and well documented in Ihara/Anderson/Deligne. Its interest is only as evidence of Grothendieck's working method in the unpublished sequel to the Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: Last line: the point is written '(-1/2,-1/2,-1)', apparently with the '1' overwritten. Mathematically it should be (-1/2,-1/2,1), as on the next page.
'en point 1/2' should read 'au point 1/2'; 's'explitant' should read 's'explicitant'.
In (328) the left vertical label is κ_{1/2} (lower-case kappa, as on the previous page), not K_{1/2}.
The equation number under 'Fermat' is overwritten; given the previous page it is most likely (322).
